lessons.title: Listening to a radio announcement
lessons.objective: Listen to a text, carry out specific tasks and answer questions about it.
lessons.course: Radio announcements give important information: who, what, where, when. We listen for key words and write short notes, not full sentences.

support.title: Radio announcement
support.text: Attention, please! The vaccination campaign against polio will take place in Mamfe from Monday 10th to Friday 14th. All children under five should be taken to the nearest health centre between 8 a.m. and 3 p.m. Vaccination is free. Bring your child’s health card.

lessons.model: The adult listens to the announcement and writes notes in a table: what, where, when, who, cost.
lessons.guided: Listen to the announcement twice. Fill a table with notes. Then tell the message to someone in your own words.
lessons.exercise: How much does the vaccination cost?
lessons.remediation: Listen for one piece of information at a time.
lessons.transfer: Listen to a radio news item at home and tell your family two pieces of information.

practice.prompt: Who should be vaccinated?
Listen and write the town.
practice.listen: Attention, please! The vaccination campaign against polio will take place in Mamfe from Monday to Friday.

practice.prompt: What must parents bring?

lessons.title: Reading meaning from pictures and signs
lessons.objective: Read the meaning expressed by pictures, symbols and signs and explain them in sentences.
lessons.course: Pictures and signs give messages without many words: a red circle with a line means “not allowed”; a battery symbol shows the charge of a phone; a green arrow shows the way out. Road signs, phone icons and posters use pictures so that everyone understands quickly.
lessons.model: The adult shows a phone screen: “This envelope means a new message. This bar shows the network.”
lessons.guided: Look at six signs and symbols (no phones in class, exit, message, low battery, no smoking, hospital). Write what each means.
lessons.exercise: What does a red circle with a line across a phone mean?
lessons.remediation: Start with signs you see every day at school.
lessons.transfer: Find three signs in your town and explain them to your family.

practice.prompt: Match each symbol with its meaning.
pairs: a green arrow over a door
practice.answer: envelope: message; arrow: exit; red cross: health.

practice.prompt: Why do signs use pictures?
Draw a sign for your classroom and write its meaning.
practice.explanation: Use a picture and few words.

lessons.title: Writing a short letter with correct punctuation
lessons.objective: Write a short friendly letter using paragraphs, capital letters and punctuation correctly.
lessons.course:
A friendly letter has: the address and the date (top right), the greeting (Dear Bih,), paragraphs (news, questions), the closing (Your friend, / Yours lovingly,) and the name.
Punctuation: capital letters for names, towns, days and the start of sentences; full stops, question marks, commas after the greeting and the closing.
lessons.model: The adult writes a letter to a cousin on the board, pointing to each part and each capital letter.
lessons.guided: Write a letter of two short paragraphs to a friend in another town. Check capitals and punctuation.
lessons.remediation: Fill in a letter template first.
lessons.transfer: Write a letter to a relative and post or send it with an adult.

practice.prompt: Put the parts of the letter in order.
practice.answer: address and date, greeting, paragraphs, closing.
practice.explanation: A letter has a fixed order.

practice.prompt: Which word needs a capital letter?
practice.explanation: Days take a capital letter: Monday.

practice.prompt: Write your letter to a friend.
practice.answer: A letter with greeting, paragraphs and closing.

lessons.title: Conditional sentences: if it rains, if I had a phone
lessons.objective: Use the first and second conditional to talk about possible and imaginary situations.
lessons.course:
First conditional — a real possibility: If + present, will + verb. “If you call me, I will answer.” “If it rains, the network will be weak.”
Second conditional — an imaginary situation: If + past, would + verb. “If I had a phone, I would call my grandmother every day.” “If I were a journalist, I would interview the mayor.”
lessons.model: The adult says: “If the battery is low, I will charge the phone. If I had a computer, I would write stories.”
lessons.guided: Complete five first-conditional sentences and write three second-conditional dreams.
lessons.exercise: Complete: If you send me a message, I … (answer).
lessons.remediation: Start with the first conditional only.
lessons.transfer: Tell your family three things you would do if you had a phone.

practice.prompt: Complete with the first conditional.
practice.text: If it [[rains]], we [[will]] stay at home.

practice.prompt: Which sentence is a second conditional?
choices: If I had a radio, I would listen to the news.
If you call, I will come.
practice.answer: If I had a radio, I would listen to the news.

practice.prompt: Write: If I had a phone, I would…

lessons.title: Perimeter and area of a triangle: a road sign
lessons.objective: Calculate the perimeter of a triangle and its area using base and height.
lessons.course:
Perimeter of a triangle = side 1 + side 2 + side 3. A triangular road sign with sides of 60 cm has a perimeter of 180 cm.
Area of a triangle = base × height ÷ 2. A triangle with base 8 cm and height 5 cm: 8 × 5 ÷ 2 = 20 cm². (It is half of a rectangle.)
lessons.model: The adult cuts a rectangle along its diagonal: two equal triangles, each half the area.
lessons.guided: Draw three triangles on squared paper. Measure the base and the height and calculate the area. Calculate the perimeter.
lessons.exercise: A triangle has a base of 10 cm and a height of 6 cm. What is its area?
lessons.remediation: Draw the rectangle around the triangle and take half.
lessons.transfer: Find triangles in signs and roofs and estimate their perimeter.

practice.prompt: A triangle has sides of 5 cm, 7 cm and 8 cm. Perimeter in cm?
Base 12 m, height 4 m. Area in m²?
A triangle is … of a rectangle with the same base and height.
practice.explanation: The diagonal cuts the rectangle in two.

lessons.title: The circle: radius, diameter and circumference
lessons.objective: Identify the radius and diameter of a circle and calculate its circumference.
lessons.course:
The radius goes from the centre to the edge. The diameter crosses the circle through the centre: diameter = 2 × radius.
The circumference is the distance round the circle: C = π × diameter, with π ≈ 3.14. A satellite dish with a diameter of 2 m has a circumference of about 3.14 × 2 = 6.28 m.
lessons.model: The adult wraps a string round a tin, unrolls it and compares it with the diameter: a little more than 3 times.
lessons.guided: Measure the diameter and the circumference of three round objects with a string. Divide C by d each time.
lessons.exercise: A circle has a radius of 5 cm. What is its diameter?
lessons.remediation: Draw circles with a compass or a string and a pencil.
lessons.transfer: Measure the circumference of a bucket or a tyre at home.

practice.prompt: A circle has a diameter of 10 cm. Circumference in cm (π ≈ 3.14)?
Match each word with its meaning.
pairs: edge to edge through the centre
practice.explanation: These are parts of a circle.

practice.prompt: The diameter is … the radius.

lessons.title: Problems in several steps: phone credit and messages
lessons.objective: Solve problems that need more than one operation.
lessons.course:
To solve a problem: read it twice, find what is asked, choose the operations, calculate step by step, and check the answer makes sense.
Example: Papa buys 2 phone cards of 1 000 frs and 1 card of 500 frs. He pays with a 5 000 frs note. Step 1: 2 × 1 000 + 500 = 2 500 frs. Step 2: 5 000 − 2 500 = 2 500 frs change.
lessons.model: The adult solves the example aloud, writing each step on a separate line.
lessons.guided: Solve four problems with two or three steps about phone credit, letters and parcels.
lessons.exercise: A message costs 25 frs. Ayuk sends 12 messages and pays with 500 frs. What is his change?
lessons.remediation: Write “Step 1” and “Step 2” and solve one at a time.
lessons.transfer: Make up a two-step problem about your family’s shopping and solve it.

practice.prompt: 3 envelopes at 150 frs and 2 stamps at 300 frs. Total in francs?

lessons.title: Reading and interpreting a table and a pictogram
lessons.objective: Read and interpret data in a table and a pictogram and solve problems with them.
lessons.course:
A pictogram uses a picture to stand for a number of things: one envelope = 10 letters. Half a picture = 5 letters.
To read it: count the pictures, multiply by the key, and compare rows.
lessons.model: The adult reads a pictogram of letters posted each day at the post office: Monday 4 envelopes = 40 letters.
lessons.guided: Read a pictogram of messages sent in a week. Answer five questions and draw your own pictogram.
lessons.exercise: One envelope = 10 letters. How many letters do 3½ envelopes show?
lessons.remediation: Count in tens with the envelopes.
lessons.transfer: Make a pictogram of the calls or messages your family receives in a week.

practice.prompt: Monday 40 letters, Tuesday 25, Wednesday 30. How many letters in the three days?
One picture = 10 letters. How many pictures for 60 letters?
Draw a pictogram with a key for a week of messages.
practice.answer: A pictogram with a key and seven rows.

lessons.title: Sources of energy and saving energy
lessons.objective: Describe sources and forms of energy, their uses and how to use energy appropriately.
lessons.course:
Energy makes things work. Sources: the sun, wind, flowing water (dams such as Song Loulou or Edéa), wood and charcoal, fuel (petrol, gas), food for our body, batteries.
Forms: heat, light, movement, sound, electricity. Solar panels change sunlight into electricity to charge phones and lamps.
We save energy: switch off lights and devices, unplug chargers, use improved cookstoves that need less wood.
lessons.model: The adult shows a small solar lamp charging in the sun, then lighting at night.
lessons.guided: List five devices at home and their energy source. Make a poster “Save energy” with three actions.
lessons.remediation: Match three sources with what they give: the sun (light and heat), wood (heat), a battery (electricity).
lessons.transfer: Switch off lights and unplug chargers at home every day this week.
lessons.materials: Pictures, a solar lamp if available.

practice.prompt: Match each source with an example of use.
practice.answer: wood: cooking; sun: drying; dam: electricity.

practice.prompt: Which action saves energy?
choices: unplug the charger when the phone is full
leave the radio on all night
practice.answer: unplug the charger when the phone is full

practice.prompt: Name one form of energy.
practice.answer: For example: heat, light or movement.

lessons.title: Écrire une carte postale ou un message
lessons.objective: Écrire un court message ou une carte postale en respectant la structure.
lessons.course: Une carte postale ou un message a : le lieu et la date, une formule d’appel (Chère Manka, / Cher Tabi,), le message (où je suis, ce que je fais, une question), une formule finale (Bisous, / À bientôt, / Amitiés,) et la signature.

support.title: Modèle
support.text:
Kribi, le 10 août
Chère Manka,
Je suis en vacances chez ma tante. La mer est belle et je nage tous les jours. Et toi, que fais-tu ?
À bientôt,
Ayuk

lessons.model: L’adulte écrit une carte postale au tableau et montre chaque partie.
lessons.guided: Écris une carte postale de quatre lignes à un ami, depuis un lieu de vacances.
lessons.exercise: Quelle formule commence une lettre à une fille ?
lessons.remediation: Complète un modèle de carte avec des étiquettes.
lessons.transfer: Écris un petit message en français à un membre de ta famille.

practice.prompt: Remets les parties dans l’ordre.
items: Je suis en vacances chez ma tante.

practice.explanation: Cher pour un garçon ; Chère pour une fille ou une femme.

lessons.title: Our national emblems: flag, seal, motto and anthem
lessons.objective: Identify the national emblems, explain their importance and show respect for them.
lessons.course:
National emblems represent the country and unite its people. The flag of Cameroon has three vertical stripes: green, red and yellow, with a yellow star in the middle of the red stripe. The motto is “Peace – Work – Fatherland”. The seal is used on official documents. The national anthem is sung at official ceremonies and at school; we stand still and attentive when it is sung.
We respect the emblems: we do not tear or misuse the flag, and we stand for the anthem.
lessons.model: At the flag-raising ceremony, the pupils stand still, the flag goes up, and everyone sings the anthem together.
lessons.guided: Draw and colour the flag of Cameroon. Write the motto. Explain how to behave during the flag ceremony.
lessons.exercise: What is the motto of Cameroon?
lessons.remediation: Learn the colours of the flag in order: green, red, yellow.
lessons.transfer: Explain the flag and the motto to a younger child.
lessons.materials: Coloured pencils, a picture of the flag.

practice.prompt: Put the colours of the flag in order from left to right.
practice.explanation: The star is on the red stripe.

practice.prompt: What do we do when the national anthem is sung?
Draw and colour the flag of Cameroon.
practice.answer: The flag with three stripes and a star.
practice.explanation: Green, red with a yellow star, yellow.

lessons.title: Weaving a paper mat to decorate the classroom
lessons.objective: Gather and treat materials and weave a mat to decorate the classroom.
lessons.course:
Weaving crosses strips over and under each other. The strips that stay fixed are the warp; the strips we pass over and under are the weft.
With paper: cut slits in a sheet (the warp), then pass coloured strips over and under. Each new strip starts the opposite way (under, then over). The same method is used with raffia or palm leaves.
lessons.model: The adult weaves three strips into a paper mat, saying “over, under, over, under”.
lessons.guided: Weave a paper mat with two colours. Display the class mats as a decoration.
lessons.exercise: What do we call the strips we pass over and under?
lessons.transfer: Ask an adult who weaves baskets or mats to show you.

practice.prompt: Complete the pattern: over, under, over, …
Match each word with its meaning.
pairs: the strips passed over and under

practice.prompt: Draw your woven mat pattern.
practice.answer: A checked pattern in two colours.

lessons.title: Performing on stage with prompts
lessons.objective: Perform on stage following different prompts and show interest in taking roles.
lessons.course:
On stage, actors follow prompts: a word, a sound, a gesture or a light that tells them when to speak or move. A narrator can give prompts. Actors stay in role, speak to the audience and do not turn their backs.
In mime, the body and face tell the message without words.
lessons.model: The adult plays narrator: “The phone rings…” — an actor answers a pretend phone; “A letter arrives…” — another reads a pretend letter.
lessons.guided: Perform a short play about messages (phone call, letter, town crier) with prompts given by a narrator. Then perform one scene in mime.
lessons.answer: A signal that tells an actor when to speak or move.
accept: a signal to speak or move
a signal that tells an actor when to speak or move

lessons.remediation: Practise one prompt and one action at a time.
lessons.transfer: Play a prompt game at home: one person gives prompts, others act.

practice.explanation: Prompts tell actors what to do.

lessons.title: Basketball: dribbling, passing and shooting
lessons.objective: Dribble, pass and shoot in basketball, following the basic rules and playing with teammates.
lessons.course: Basketball: two teams of five players. We move with the ball by dribbling (bouncing it with one hand); we may not walk with the ball in our hands. We pass to teammates (chest pass, bounce pass) and shoot at the basket. A normal basket gives 2 points; a shot from far (behind the three-point line) gives 3.
lessons.model: The adult dribbles with the fingertips, looking up, then makes a chest pass.
lessons.guided: Dribble round cones with each hand. Practise chest and bounce passes. Shoot at a basket or a target.
lessons.exercise: How many points does a normal basket give?
lessons.transfer: Play a passing game with friends without walking with the ball.
lessons.materials: A ball, cones or stones, a basket or target.

choices: by walking with it in our hands
practice.explanation: Walking with the ball is not allowed.

lessons.title: A conversation in the family language
lessons.objective: Handle a short conversation in the family language and read simple words with special letters.
lessons.course:
A conversation has steps: greet, ask how the other person is, talk about a subject (the market, the weather, school), answer questions and say goodbye.
Some Cameroonian languages use letters of the General Alphabet such as ɛ, ɔ, ŋ and tone marks. We learn to read simple words with them with an adult.
lessons.model: The adult and the child have a short conversation in the family language about the day.
lessons.guided: Prepare and act a conversation of six exchanges in the family language with an adult. Read three words with special letters.
lessons.exercise: What is the last step of a conversation?
lessons.remediation: Practise the greeting and the goodbye first.
lessons.transfer: Have a conversation in the family language with a grandparent.
lessons.materials: An adult who speaks the language.

practice.prompt: Put the conversation in order.
Which letter belongs to the General Alphabet of Cameroonian Languages but not to the English alphabet?

lessons.title: Credible information and responsible social media
lessons.objective: Select credible sources of information, cite them, and use social media responsibly while respecting privacy.
lessons.course:
Not all information on the internet is true. A credible source is known and serious: an official website, a school book, a recognised newspaper, a health ministry. Check: Who wrote it? Is it recent? Do other serious sources say the same? Write the name of the source when you use information.
Social media connect people, but many platforms are only for users of 13 years or more. With an adult: never share your address, school or photos with strangers, do not share false news, be kind, and tell an adult if something worries you.
lessons.model: The adult compares two messages about a disease: one from the health ministry, one from an unknown forwarded message.
lessons.guided: Look at three pieces of information with an adult and decide which is credible and why. Make a list of four rules for social media.
lessons.exercise: Name one question to check if information is credible.
lessons.remediation: Learn one question first: Who wrote it?
lessons.transfer: Before sharing a message, check it with an adult.
lessons.materials: Printed examples of messages and websites.

practice.prompt: Which source is the most credible about vaccines?
Which behaviour respects privacy?
choices: not sharing a friend’s photo without permission
practice.answer: not sharing a friend’s photo without permission

practice.prompt: Write four rules for using social media safely.
practice.explanation: Privacy, kindness, truth, ask an adult.
